title: Persistent causal detector-cluster tracker preflight

scope.identity: Assign stable persistent identifiers to snapshot components across monotone causal prefixes.
scope.ownership: Record each event's immutable origin identifier while maintaining a current canonical owner after merges.
scope.merges: When a new event joins prior components, merge deterministically into the earliest persistent identifier and retain aliases.
scope.geometry: Refresh snapshot age, extent, separation, nearest active absorber, and link candidates at every prefix.
scope.schedule_handoff: Use the persistent identifier when a tracked component touches the current detector frontier.
not_in_scope: event deletion or retrospective rewrite in the raw observation record
proof that the registered radius-one adjacency is physically optimal
microscopic D(S3), noisy D4, schedule performance, threshold, or fault tolerance

invariants: prefix horizons are monotone and previously observed events remain unchanged
each new event receives one immutable origin cluster identifier
a component overlapping one prior cluster retains its identifier
a component overlapping multiple prior clusters chooses the earliest identifier deterministically and records all aliases
fixed-radius append-only components may merge but never split
current ownership is total and agrees with the active persistent components
geometry and absorber candidates are refreshed from the current causal prefix
schedule handoff exposes only current-frontier detector vertices under the persistent identifier

verified_cases: a component retains its persistent identifier when a new event extends it
a disconnected new component receives a new identifier
a bridge event merges two components into the earliest identifier while preserving an alias and immutable event origins
removed or changed historical detector events are rejected
an idempotent same-prefix refresh does not duplicate event origins
absorber candidates refresh after lifecycle changes and exclude a persistent-ID-owned absorber
the persistent identifier drives the public current-frontier schedule handoff

claim_boundary: This verifies deterministic state management over the registered snapshot rule. It does not license record deletion, establish the physical clustering rule, or provide noisy-channel or threshold evidence.
next_gate: After persistent tracking passes, audit the remaining J1/J2 prerequisites and register the smallest shared-fault-history scheduling baseline matrix before introducing new physics claims.
